logic.top_level: pathways: one block per procedure, plus a catch-all 'surgical treatment ... that does not meet the criteria above does not meet the definition of medical necessity'
logic.exclusions_or_contraindications: No contraindication list. Exclusions are an 'experimental or investigational' list of procedures; 'snoring alone is not considered a medical condition'.
logic.initial_vs_repeat: HGNS 'Revision/Replacement ... meets the definition of medical necessity when all of the criteria above are met, the device is not functioning and is no longer under warranty.' Oral appliances limited to one per 12 months (Reimbursement).

and_or_ambiguity.quote: For members with mild to moderate obstructive sleep apnea; OR For members with severe obstructive sleep apnea who have failed a trial of continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) or is contraindicated AND The device is prescribed by a treating physician, the device is custom-fitted ... AND there is absence of temporomandibular dysfunction or periodontal disease
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Layout puts 'AND' on its own line before the device bullet; reading is (mild-moderate OR (severe AND CPAP failed/contraindicated)) AND device conditions, but the structure is only implied by indentation.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: in appropriately select members who have failed an adequate trial of CPAP OR failed an adequate trial of an oral appliance
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: UPPP needs only ONE of CPAP or oral appliance failure; hyoid/MMA similarly 'have not responded to or do not tolerate CPAP OR failed an adequate trial of an oral appliance'. Cigna requires both PAP and consideration of an appliance.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Mild to Moderate ... AHI, REI, or RDI of 15 or more events per hour, OR ... 5 or more events per hour in a member with one or more signs or symptoms
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: 'Mild to moderate' is defined with a floor of 15 and no ceiling, so it overlaps 'Severe' (> 30). A patient with AHI 45 satisfies both definitions. Also, 'mild' (AHI 5-14) without symptoms is not covered by the definition.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: CPAP failure (residual AHI >= 15 or failure to use CPAP >= 4 hr per night for >= 5 nights per week) or inability to tolerate CPAP
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Nested or inside an item that sits inside an ALL list; also 'residual AHI >= 15' is measured on-treatment, a different measurement from the baseline AHI in the previous bullet.

extraction_hazards: Definitions are far from the criteria that use them and must be joined
Descriptive prose in Description mentions procedures and statements (e.g. 'insufficient evidence') that look like coverage language
Investigational and medically-necessary procedures interleaved in one CPT list with the word '(Investigational)' inline on some rows
Special characters >= and <= (and unicode) in HGNS block
LOINC table at end is documentation guidance in table form
Unmarked word-wrap inside nested bullets (o markers)
Long CPT table splits across a page without repeated headers
interesting_structures: Two-population HGNS (adult; Down syndrome adolescent) with separate AHI and BMI rules (percentile BMI)
Severity definitions embedded in a Definitions section; pediatric severity differs
Procedure-level OR between 'CPAP failed' and 'oral appliance failed' rather than requiring both
Reimbursement frequency limit; documentation recency via LOINC time frames

fit_to_tree.scale: 1 = all/any/not expresses it cleanly ... 5 = needs new constructs or human judgment
fit_to_tree.why: Each HGNS block is a clean all-of with numeric leaves, but conventional surgery relies on loose terms ('adequate trial', 'appropriately selected') and a definition with overlapping ranges. Population branching (adult/pediatric) is pathway-style.
